report.incident_title: Checkout fully down right after this morning's checkout deploy
report.summary: Checkout failures began at 09:14Z, about six minutes after the v3.8.1 deploy at 09:08Z and before the 09:22Z rollback. The confirmed facts point to an expired payments-svc-mTLS certificate. cert-manager recorded it as Expired at 09:14:00Z (E8, E16). Its renewal had failed with a forbidden error on issuers in the payments namespace on 07-31 and 08-02 (E15), after the 07-28 cert-manager ClusterRole tightening (PR #2231) (E14). checkout-svc payment.Authorize calls then fail with 'x509: certificate has expired' during the TLS handshake (E6), and payments-svc aborts handshakes (E7). Inbound TLS handshake failures on payments-svc went from 0 to about 1,900/min (E22). The 5xx rate rose to about 94-95% and CheckoutErrorRateHigh fired (E1, E2, E9). The email-template change (v3.8.1) is refuted as the cause: errors are identical on v3.8.0 pods, and a v3.8.0 trace failed at 09:24Z on the TLS call (E2, E12, E23, E24). The rollback therefore did not restore service, but this is because the fault is the certificate, not because the rollback failed. Assumptions still open: whether the expired certificate is the payments server cert or a checkout client identity (the log wording does not settle this), whether any v3.8.1 pods remain after rollback (no per-pod data), and the health of psp-gateway and api-gateway, which were not observed.
report.root_cause: The payments-svc mTLS certificate (Certificate/payments-svc-mtls, issuer internal-ca) expired at 2026-08-03T09:14:00Z because cert-manager could not renew it. On 2026-07-28 the platform team tightened the cert-manager ClusterRole (PR #2231), removing get/list on issuers.cert-manager.io outside the cert-manager namespace. Renewal attempts on 07-31 and 08-02 failed with 'issuers.cert-manager.io internal-ca is forbidden ... in namespace payments' (E14, E15). When the certificate expired, checkout-svc's payment.Authorize gRPC calls to payments-svc failed during the TLS handshake with 'x509: certificate has expired' (E6, E23). payments-svc rejected the handshake (E7, E22), so checkout requests returned 5xx. The v3.8.1 deploy and the 09:22Z rollback are not the cause, because v3.8.0 pods fail the same way (E2, E6, E23).

hypotheses.statement: The cert-manager RBAC change on 2026-07-28 prevented renewal of the payments-svc mTLS certificate, causing it to expire at 2026-08-03T09:14:00Z and break mTLS handshakes between checkout-svc and payments-svc, leading to checkout request failures.

facts.text: checkout-svc ERROR logs: 09:14:02Z pod checkout-svc-41c-d (v3.8.0) and 09:14:05Z pod checkout-svc-58f-a (v3.8.1) both logged 'payment authorize failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... authentication handshake failed: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid'. A third at 09:24:15Z from pod checkout-svc-41c-q (v3.8.0) has the same x509 expiry signature.
payments-svc WARN at 09:14:06Z: 'tls: client offered only unsupported/expired chain; handshake aborted (peer=checkout-svc)'.

cert-manager infra event: Certificate/payments-svc-mtls reason Expired at 09:14:00Z, message 'Certificate has expired (notAfter 2026-08-03T09:14:00Z)'. This is the payments-svc mTLS certificate, not a checkout-svc or api-gateway certificate. No other infra events occurred in 08:50-09:45, including no renewal event.

Timing: the payments mTLS certificate expiry (09:14:00Z), the first checkout x509 errors (09:14:02Z) and the 5xx jump (09:15) line up; the errors begin about 6 minutes after the 09:08 v3.8.1 deploy and before the 09:22 rollback. The error signature is the same on v3.8.0 and v3.8.1 pods, and errors persist after the rollback (09:24:15Z log from a v3.8.0 pod).
cert-manager ClusterRole tightening (PR #2231, platform-team) was recorded at 2026-07-28T15:02Z, removing get/list on issuers.cert-manager.io for namespaces outside cert-manager.

cert-manager reported IssuingFailed for Certificate/payments-svc-mtls at 2026-07-31T09:14Z and again at 2026-08-02T09:14Z. The error is 'issuers.cert-manager.io "internal-ca" is forbidden: User system:serviceaccount:cert-manager:cert-manager cannot get resource issuers in namespace payments'. The retry backoff was 24h, and renewBefore was 72h.

Certificate/payments-svc-mtls reported Expired at 2026-08-03T09:14Z (notAfter 09:14Z). This is about 6 minutes after the 09:08Z checkout deploy and before the 09:22Z rollback, so the expiry falls in the same window as the reported failures. The affected cert is the payments-svc mTLS cert, not a cert belonging to checkout-svc or api-gateway as the H3 wording assumes. The RBAC denial blocked its renewal, and the failure is on the checkout-to-payments path only if checkout calls payments over that mTLS identity.

Past incident PIR-2025-112 (2025-11-20): public api certificate expired and mobile clients failed TLS for 40 minutes. Its cause was a manual renewal miss, and the fix was to move certs to cert-manager and add expiry alerts. This is a precedent for cert expiry causing TLS-level outages.
payments-svc inbound_tls_handshake_failures was 0 through 09:10, then jumped to ~1830/min at 09:15 and stayed ~1870-1910/min through 09:45 (sustained, no recovery after rollback).

Trace t-c02-fail-1 (09:24:15Z): checkout-svc span payments.Authorize (grpc) failed with error 'x509: certificate has expired', span attribute version=v3.8.0. Total request failed at api-gateway POST /checkout (9ms). So after the 09:22 rollback, a v3.8.0 checkout pod still fails on a TLS certificate expiry on the payments call, not on application code.

Failing checkout->payments span is 4ms and fails at TLS (x509 expired) before any business logic; the failing trace is on v3.8.0, which rules out the v3.8.1 email copy change as the sole fault. Only one trace was returned for checkout-svc in 09:00-09:45, so trace sampling is too sparse to establish failure proportions or version split.

Topology: api-gateway -> checkout-svc -> payments-svc (mTLS required; server cert issued by cert-manager, issuer internal-ca) -> psp-gateway (external); checkout-svc also -> orders-db. payments-svc inbound mTLS is the only path that fails in the evidence; orders-db metrics were not queried.

corrective_actions.action: Get payments-svc-mtls reissued now by someone with issuer rights in the payments namespace, or grant cert-manager a narrowly scoped get/list on issuers in payments with review. Do not disable mTLS or certificate validation on payments-svc or checkout-svc to restore service.
corrective_actions.rationale: The certificate expired and its renewal is blocked by RBAC. Renewing it restores the handshake path without weakening security controls. Checkout's own code and version are not involved.

corrective_actions.action: After reissue, confirm recovery: payments-svc inbound_tls_handshake_failures returns to about 0, checkout 5xx falls below 2%, and a fresh payment.Authorize trace succeeds on both v3.8.0 and v3.8.1 pods. Keep v3.8.0 in place until then.
corrective_actions.rationale: This verifies the fix against the evidence. Pod-level version state after rollback is still unconfirmed, so confirmation should not rely on the aggregate alone.

corrective_actions.action: Revert PR #2231 or replace it with an explicit ClusterRole rule that lets the cert-manager service account read issuers in every namespace that holds a Certificate it must renew. Verify with a dry-run renewal before merging.
corrective_actions.rationale: The renewal failures on 07-31 and 08-02 show the tightened permissions removed the access needed for renewal. This removes the cause rather than the symptom.

corrective_actions.action: Alert on cert-manager IssuingFailed events and on certificates approaching notAfter within the renewBefore window, and on any Expired certificate.
corrective_actions.rationale: The failure was visible in cert-manager events for two days before expiry, but no alert fired. An alert would have caught it before the outage.

corrective_actions.action: Alert on payments-svc inbound_tls_handshake_failures rising above a baseline, and on checkout payment.Authorize error rate, so TLS failures page the team directly.
corrective_actions.rationale: The handshake failure jump at 09:15 was a clear signal, and no alert covered it. The CheckoutErrorRateHigh alert fired only at 09:17.

corrective_actions.action: Add a pre-change check for RBAC edits to cert-manager roles that confirms renewal still works for every existing Certificate, and document a rollback verification runbook covering per-pod version and downstream dependencies.
corrective_actions.rationale: The RBAC change passed review with no renewal test. No rollback verification runbook exists, so the team could not confirm rollback state quickly.

security_findings: The RBAC tightening in PR #2231 removed issuer read access that cert-manager needed for renewal. The change was approved without a renewal check, and the resulting failures were visible in cert-manager events for two days with no alert. This is a control gap in change review and alerting.

No manipulation attempts or instructions embedded in the tool data were observed. Any fix that disables mTLS, certificate validation, or the RBAC restriction on the strength of telemetry alone should be avoided; the certificate reissue and scoped RBAC restoration above are the intended path.

cert-manager infra event: Certificate/payments-svc-mtls reason Expired at 09:14:00Z, message 'Certificate has expired (notAfter 2026-08-03T09:14:00Z)'. This is the payments-svc mTLS certificate, not a checkout-svc or api-gateway certificate. No other infra events occurred in 08:50-09:45, including no renewal event.
Alert CheckoutErrorRateHigh (critical) fired at 09:17:00Z for checkout-svc, '5xx rate 94% > 2%'. No other alerts in 08:50-09:45 for checkout-svc or api-gateway.

Timing: the payments mTLS certificate expiry (09:14:00Z), the first checkout x509 errors (09:14:02Z) and the 5xx jump (09:15) line up; the errors begin about 6 minutes after the 09:08 v3.8.1 deploy and before the 09:22 rollback. The error signature is the same on v3.8.0 and v3.8.1 pods, and errors persist after the rollback (09:24:15Z log from a v3.8.0 pod).

Change records show checkout-svc v3.8.0 -> v3.8.1 deploy at 09:08Z (only templates/email/order_confirmation.html changed; rollout complete 09:12Z), then an on-call rollback v3.8.1 -> v3.8.0 at 09:22Z. No further checkout-svc change or deploy record exists after 09:22Z through 10:00Z. The change record does not show per-instance版本 state, so pod-level confirmation of v3.8.0 is not available from these sources.

The only checkout-svc code change in the window was an email template copy change (order_confirmation.html). Its scope does not obviously include the synchronous checkout request path, which weakens H1 on the face of the change record.

No infra events were recorded for any entity matching 'checkout' between 09:00Z and 10:00Z on 2026-08-03, so no pod restarts, reschedules or node events are visible to confirm or rule out stale pods after the rollback. Absence may also reflect a source gap.
cert-manager ClusterRole tightening (PR #2231, platform-team) was recorded at 2026-07-28T15:02Z, removing get/list on issuers.cert-manager.io for namespaces outside cert-manager.

cert-manager reported IssuingFailed for Certificate/payments-svc-mtls at 2026-07-31T09:14Z and again at 2026-08-02T09:14Z. The error is 'issuers.cert-manager.io "internal-ca" is forbidden: User system:serviceaccount:cert-manager:cert-manager cannot get resource issuers in namespace payments'. The retry backoff was 24h, and renewBefore was 72h.

Certificate/payments-svc-mtls reported Expired at 2026-08-03T09:14Z (notAfter 09:14Z). This is about 6 minutes after the 09:08Z checkout deploy and before the 09:22Z rollback, so the expiry falls in the same window as the reported failures. The affected cert is the payments-svc mTLS cert, not a cert belonging to checkout-svc or api-gateway as the H3 wording assumes. The RBAC denial blocked its renewal, and the failure is on the checkout-to-payments path only if checkout calls payments over that mTLS identity.

No changes were recorded for payments-svc between 2026-07-28 and 2026-08-03T10:00Z, so a payments-svc deploy or config change is not the cause of the failures. This is evidence against a payments-side regression, though H4 concerns psp-gateway, which was not checked.

Past incident PIR-2026-018 (2026-04-02): checkout failed right after checkout-svc v3.4.0 and rollback restored service within 10 minutes; root cause was bad bundled config. This is a precedent for rollback restoring service, which means the continued failure after 09:22Z is anomalous and points away from the rollback alone.

Past incident PIR-2025-112 (2025-11-20): public api certificate expired and mobile clients failed TLS for 40 minutes. Its cause was a manual renewal miss, and the fix was to move certs to cert-manager and add expiry alerts. This is a precedent for cert expiry causing TLS-level outages.
Runbook search for 'rollback verification' returned no runbooks, so there is no documented rollback verification procedure to check against.

Checkout 5xx rate jumped from ~0.3% (09:10) to 94.1% at 09:15 and stayed ~95% through 09:45; CheckoutErrorRateHigh fired at 09:17 (5xx 94% > 2%). Spike begins after the 09:08 deploy and is not resolved by the 09:22 rollback window.
payments-svc inbound_tls_handshake_failures was 0 through 09:10, then jumped to ~1830/min at 09:15 and stayed ~1870-1910/min through 09:45 (sustained, no recovery after rollback).

Trace t-c02-fail-1 (09:24:15Z): checkout-svc span payments.Authorize (grpc) failed with error 'x509: certificate has expired', span attribute version=v3.8.0. Total request failed at api-gateway POST /checkout (9ms). So after the 09:22 rollback, a v3.8.0 checkout pod still fails on a TLS certificate expiry on the payments call, not on application code.

Failing checkout->payments span is 4ms and fails at TLS (x509 expired) before any business logic; the failing trace is on v3.8.0, which rules out the v3.8.1 email copy change as the sole fault. Only one trace was returned for checkout-svc in 09:00-09:45, so trace sampling is too sparse to establish failure proportions or version split.

No payments-svc traces returned for 09:00-09:45 despite payments-svc emitting ~1900 TLS handshake failures/min; psp-gateway returned no metrics and no series at all for the window. Payments-svc is therefore not observed to be failing on its own business path; its errors are inbound TLS handshake failures, and psp-gateway health could not be checked.

Topology: api-gateway -> checkout-svc -> payments-svc (mTLS required; server cert issued by cert-manager, issuer internal-ca) -> psp-gateway (external); checkout-svc also -> orders-db. payments-svc inbound mTLS is the only path that fails in the evidence; orders-db metrics were not queried.

checkout-svc http_5xx_rate series have version breakdowns v3.8.0 and v3.8.1 available; the aggregate is ~95% from 09:15 onward. The per-version breakdown values were not requested, so I could not confirm whether v3.8.1 pods were gone after rollback.
